title: NEB Class 11 Biology — Faunal Diversity — 2024
subject: biology
source: NEB Grade 11 Model Questions / NEB Past Papers 2020-2024

questions.question: Write the diagnostic features of the phylum Arthropoda. Give one example.
questions.solution:
Jointed appendages; **chitinous exoskeleton**; segmented body (head–thorax–abdomen); open circulation; tracheal/gill respiration.

Example: *Periplaneta* (cockroach), prawn, king crab — the largest animal phylum (~75% of known species are insects).
questions.knowledgeNote: Moulting (ecdysis) is the price of armour — growth happens only between sheds.

questions.question: Describe the respiratory system of frog.
questions.solution:
**Cutaneous** (moist skin — underwater/hibernation), **buccal** (mouth-cavity pumping), **pulmonary** (paired sac-like lungs on land).

Frogs ventilate by **positive pressure**: mouth fills with air, nostrils shut, buccal floor forces air into the lungs.
questions.knowledgeNote: Tadpoles breathe with gills — metamorphosis rebuilds the whole respiratory toolkit.

questions.question: Write the general characters of phylum Mollusca with two examples.
questions.solution:
Soft unsegmented body in three parts (head – visceral mass – muscular foot); usually a calcareous **shell**; mantle cavity with gills; open circulation (except cephalopods).

Examples: *Pila* (apple snail), *Unio* (freshwater mussel), octopus.
questions.knowledgeNote: Second-largest phylum — pearls are nacre-coated irritants, the oyster's defence turned luxury.

questions.question: Distinguish between chordates and non-chordates.
questions.solution:
**Chordates** have (at some stage) a notochord, dorsal hollow nerve cord, pharyngeal gill slits, and a post-anal tail — e.g. fish, frog, humans.

**Non-chordates** lack all four — e.g. earthworm, snail, starfish. Chordates are mostly bilateral with closed circulation; non-chordates far more diverse in symmetry and systems.
questions.knowledgeNote: Human gill slits appear only as embryos — ontogeny briefly replays phylogeny.

questions.question: Write the general characters of phylum Annelida with one example.
questions.solution:
True segmentation (**metamerism**), closed circulation, setae/chaetae for movement, moist cuticle, hermaphroditic.

Example: *Pheretima* (earthworm) — the soil's ploughman.
questions.knowledgeNote: Metamerism (repeated segments) prefigures the vertebrate backbone's serial plan.

questions.question: What is the water vascular system? In which phylum is it found? Write its functions.
questions.solution:
Found in **Echinodermata** (starfish): seawater-filled canals ending in suckered **tube feet**, worked by ampullae.

Functions: locomotion, food capture, respiration, and excretion — hydraulics instead of muscles.
questions.knowledgeNote: Radial symmetry in adults but bilateral larvae — echinoderms evolved *back* to radial from bilateral ancestors.
